blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Deductions and exemptions reduce the tax you pay — and they are legal. A deduction is something you subtract from your taxable income before the tax is calculated. Pension contributions, charity donations, and some business expenses can all be deductions.

An exemption is even stronger. It removes an item from the calculation entirely. Certain small incomes, certain benefits, and certain kinds of gift are simply exempt. They do not count.

Used correctly, deductions and exemptions are not aggressive tax tricks. They are rules the government put in place to encourage good behaviour. Using them is often exactly what the system is designed for.

items.q: What is a deduction?
options: A benefit only rich people can use
Something you subtract from your taxable income before the tax is calculated
A gift you give to the government
A tax the government adds at the end
items.why: "A deduction is something you subtract from your taxable income before the tax is calculated."

items.q: What does an exemption do?
options: It sends the money to charity
It removes an item from the calculation entirely
It doubles the tax on an item
It moves an item to next year
items.why: "An exemption… removes an item from the calculation entirely."

items.q: Which of these can be a deduction?
options: A phone call to a friend
items.why: "Pension contributions, charity donations, and some business expenses can all be deductions."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: Using deductions and exemptions is an aggressive trick to cheat the system
Deductions are legal ways to reduce tax
The government created these rules on purpose
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que NÃO são truques agressivos — são regras do próprio governo.

items.q: The text suggests that the government wants people to…
options: pay as much tax as possible
use these rules and behave in good ways
items.why: Inferência: as regras existem "to encourage good behaviour" — o governo quer que as pessoas as usem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie falando com uma nova cliente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, thanks for coming in. Let me show you two easy ways to pay less tax this year — both fully legal, don't worry.

First, your pension. If you put a little more into your pension this year, we can use it as a deduction. That means we subtract it from your taxable income. Your income on paper goes down, so your tax goes down too. It is that simple.

Second, charity. I saw that you gave some money to a charity last month. Good news — that donation can also be a deduction. If you send me the receipt, I will add it to your file.

These are not tricks. They are normal rules. The government made them to encourage people to save for the future and to help others. So really, you are just using the system the way it was designed. Many people are afraid to use them, but they should not be.

If you bring me both receipts by Friday, we will finish everything before the deadline. Then you can relax and enjoy your weekend.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Sophie helping the client do?
options: Pay less tax this year, legally
items.why: "two easy ways to pay less tax this year — both fully legal."

items.q: What happens if the client puts more into her pension?
items.why: "we subtract it from your taxable income. Your income on paper goes down."

items.q: What does Sophie ask the client to bring?
items.why: "If you bring me both receipts by Friday, we will finish everything."

items.q: Sophie says these are "not tricks." What does she mean?
options: They only work for big companies
They are normal, legal rules made by the government
items.why: Inferência: ela explica que são regras normais criadas pelo governo — nada escondido ou errado.

items.q: How does Sophie most likely want the client to feel?
options: Calm and safe about the process
items.why: Inferência: ela repete "don't worry", "it is that simple" e "then you can relax" — quer tranquilizar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her pension counts as a deduction." A deduction is…
options: something you subtract from your taxable income
an extra tax you must pay
items.why: Deduction = dedução: algo que você subtrai da renda tributável.

items.q: "This small gift is exempt." This means it…
options: must be reported to the police
is worth a lot of money
does not count in the tax calculation
items.why: Exemption/exempt = isenção/isento: o item sai do cálculo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ the donation from her income before we count the tax."
items.why: To subtract = subtrair: tirar um valor do total.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "After the deduction, her ___ was much lower, so she paid less tax."
items.why: Taxable income = renda tributável: o valor sobre o qual o imposto é calculado.

items.q: "A charity donation can lower your tax." A charity donation is…
options: money you keep in your pocket
money you give to help others
money you win in a game
money you borrow from a bank
items.why: Charity donation = doação a caridade: dinheiro dado para ajudar outras pessoas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando falamos de impostos e trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the tax report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Please fill in this form with your income." To fill in means to…
items.why: Fill in = preencher: escrever as informações pedidas.

items.q: "The deadline is close, so we need to hurry up." To hurry up means to…
items.why: Hurry up = apressar-se, ir mais rápido.

items.q: "Sophie will look into the new tax rule." To look into means to…
items.why: Look into = investigar, examinar com atenção.

items.q: "Don't worry, the tax office will sort out the mistake." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, arrumar o problema.
